notes: Trigger cases only. Every skill in the claude/workflow group is installed for
every case, because a group is the unit people install -- so a case can fail by
the wrong sibling firing, not just by silence.
The should_not_trigger arm is mostly other members of this group. These skills
are adjacent by design (plan/execute/delegate, request/receive review), so the
queries that discriminate between them are the ones worth measuring. Obvious
non-matches would report a precision none of them has earned.
should_trigger: Keep running the tests and fixing failures until they all pass.
Iterate on the query until it runs under 200ms.
Retry this until the build is green, however many attempts it takes.
Optimise this function until the benchmark target is met.
Loop on it: fix, run, repeat, until nothing fails.
Just keep going until the flaky test stops flaking.
Work at this by trial and error until the metric hits the threshold.
Grind on this until it's done -- I don't need a plan, just results.
should_not_trigger: Run the tests once and tell me what fails.
Write a plan for fixing these failures.
Work through the written plan with review checkpoints.
The branch is done and green. Merge or PR?
Set up pytest for this project.
Explain what a flaky test is.
